v9_champion_baseline.description: 88% CatBoost Depth 4 (5 seeds) + 12% Logistic Regression on 90 features

combined_expert_system.interpretation: Training experts exclusively on partitioned subsets starves the model of shared behavioral interactions, reducing performance if used standalone (especially for Annual which has only 29% of rows).

central_only_peak.observation: Central-only correction consistently improves all 3 temporal folds (F1 +18 bps, F2 +38 bps, F3 +22 bps).

joint_peak.observation: Joint correction (Central + Annual) on Global Depth-3 yields +40 bps over Depth-3 baseline.

best_standalone_tree_candidate.name: 75% Global Depth-3 + 25% Billing Expert + Joint Residual Correction (alpha=0.50)

best_overall_ensemble_candidate.name: 88% (75/25 Depth-3 Expert + Joint Residual 0.50) + 12% Logistic Regression

strategic_conclusion.gap_reduction: Reduced gap from 0.00165 (V13) down to 0.00081 (V14), capturing +9.5 bps in mean CV.
strategic_conclusion.key_learning: Partitioning the dataset entirely into separate expert models starves the smaller cohort (annual, 29% of data). However, ensembling a 25% slice of the expert into the Global model captures specialized separation while retaining full-dataset generalization (+22 bps lift). Furthermore, training-only residual correction for the central region and annual billing removes systematic miscalibration (+34 bps lift). Finally, regularized linear modeling provides orthogonal inductive bias (+28 bps lift).
strategic_conclusion.recommended_v15_direction: To bridge the remaining 0.00081 gap: (1) Sample-weighting rather than subset-partitioning for annual subscribers (avoiding sample starvation); (2) LightGBM / XGBoost Depth-3 counterpart models to diversify the tree ensemble beyond CatBoost; (3) Stacking meta-learner trained on OOF predictions across the 3 diverse model families.
